2. The only ground upon which the claim for pre-emption was disallowed by the lower appellate court was that it was barred by limitation having been filed after more than four months from the date of the knowledge of the impugned transfer of land by the co-sharer concerned as contemplated under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In this connection it may be mentioned that the pre-emption was claimed by a minor female child through her mother as the natural and legal guardian and next friend. It was alleged that the pre-emption co-sharer being a minor female notice of the transfer was served in the name of the said female minor at the residence of her maternal uncle and that her mother was living with her step-father in whose residence the minor female was also residing. The trial court held that in such circumstances it could not be said that the pre-emptor and her natural and legal guardian being the next friend had no knowledge about the service of the notice of transfer, but the lower appellate court held otherwise that the mother of the minor female who claimed the pre-emption on behalf of the female minor as natural and legal guardian and next friend had knowledge about the service of notice of the transfer at the residence of the maternal uncle of the female child immediately after the execution and registration of the impugned deed of transfer and on that account when the pre-emption case was filed after 7 years from the date of the service of the notice of transfer the pre-emption case was evidently barred by limitation under Section 96(1) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The finding of the lower appellate court on the issue of limitation has been decided as a question of fact based upon the evidence on record and the lower appellate court as a first court of appeal and final court of fact having all the co-lateral power of the trial court could believe or disbelieve any evidence and the finding as the issue of limitation having been made in that manner, in the absence of any error of law in such finding, it must be presumed to be a conclave one without warranting any interference by this Court exercising its discretionary revisional jurisdiction. 

 3. A question however has been raised in this Rule at to whether the knowledge of natural and legal guardian of a minor female as a next friend in the pre emption proceeding can be said to be knowledge of the minor female being the actual co-sharer pre-emptor and consequently whether the period of limitation for instituting a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act can be extended till the attainment of majority of the minor female for the purpose of claiming pre-emption. On this question the court felt the necessity of some assistance from a senior member of the Bar and consequently requested Mr. Rafiqur Rahman to appear as Amicus Curiae to assist the court on this question. Mr. Rafiqur Rahman has drawn the notice of the court to relevant sections 6, 8 and 29 of the Limitation Act and also cited a decision reported in PLD 1952 Dacca 79 by Ibrahim, J. and also another decision reported in 55 C.W N. 501 by Lahiri, J. Section 6(1) of Limitation Act says that where a person entitled to institute a proceeding is a minor at the time from which the period of limitation is to be reckoned be may institute such proceeding after such disability has ceased. Section 8 of the Limitation Act however specifically makes an exception stating that Section 6 as aforesaid shall not apply to enforce right of pre-emption. Section 29 (2) of the Limitation Act further says that where any special law prescribes a special period of limitation, it shall apply accordingly and for the purpose of determining the period the provisions of sections 4-9-18 and 22 of the Limitation Act shall apply and the remaining provisions of the Limitation Act shall not apply. Considering the aforesaid provisions of sections 6 (1), 8 and 29(2) of the Limitation Act it clearly appears that the provision for secession of disability of a minor for the purpose of instituting any proceeding shall not apply in case of pre-emption even under a special law like section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. That being so, if there being any delay in instituting a pre-emption case by a minor female, the period of limitation cannot be extended and condoned on that account. Further, when a minor sues through her natural and legal guardian being a mother as a next friend, the knowledge of the mother as guardian shall be deemed to be the knowledge of the minor.
